title: "Analysis"

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)

climate <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "02_cleaned_data.rds"))
eda <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "03_eda_results.rds"))
quality <- read_csv(here("output", "tables", "data_quality.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Pipeline

| Step | Script | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Load | `scripts/01_data_loading.R` | Reads the three station exports (long format: one row per timestamp and variable) |
| Clean | `scripts/02_data_cleaning.R` | Parses and rounds timestamps to the hour, pivots to one row per station-hour, applies range checks and detects faulty sensors |
| Analyse | `scripts/03_eda.R` | City comparison on the common period, daily cycles, daily temperature range, correlations, extremes |
| Plot | `scripts/04_visualizations.R` | All figures in `output/figures/` |

`Rscript run_all.R` runs the four steps; `quarto render` builds this site.

## 2. Data cleaning

**Timestamps.** Readings arrive on the hour, sometimes a few seconds late (`07:00:02`), so they are rounded to the hour before reshaping. Midnight timestamps needed care: converting them back to text drops the time part, which silently lost 310 midnight readings in an earlier version of this analysis.

**Range checks.** Values outside physical limits (temperature outside −20 to 60 °C, humidity outside 0 to 100 %, wind above 60 m/s, solar above 1,400 W/m²) are set to missing. None were found.

**Sensor fault detection.** A working solar sensor reads close to 0 W/m² at night. Each station's median reading between 20:00 and 05:00 is checked:

```{r solar-check}
quality %>%
  transmute(Station = city,
            `Median night-time solar (W/m²)` = round(median_night_solar, 1),
            Verdict = if_else(solar_sensor_ok, "OK", "Faulty: solar readings removed")) %>%
  kable()
```

Kef's sensor reports 945 to 958 W/m² around the clock, so all its solar values are excluded. Without this check, Kef would appear to receive ten times more sunlight than the coastal stations.

**Common period.** The stations cover different dates (Sousse runs until 6 January), so cities are compared only on the hours between `r format(eda$common_start, "%d %b %H:%M")` and `r format(eda$common_end, "%d %b %Y %H:%M")`.

## 3. City comparison (common period)

```{r city-stats}
eda$city_stats %>%
  transmute(Station = city, `Hours` = hours,
            `Mean temp (°C)` = avg_temp, `Min (°C)` = min_temp, `Max (°C)` = max_temp,
            `Mean humidity (%)` = avg_humidity, `Mean dew point (°C)` = avg_dew_point,
            `Mean wind (m/s)` = avg_wind, `Max wind (m/s)` = max_wind) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r hour-counts}
eda$hour_counts %>%
  transmute(Station = city, Hours = hours,
            `Hours below 5 °C` = hours_below_5c,
            `Hours above 80 % humidity` = hours_above_80pct_humidity,
            `Share humid (%)` = pct_humid,
            `Calm hours (< 2 m/s)` = calm_hours,
            `Share calm (%)` = pct_calm) %>%
  kable()
```

## 4. Daily temperature range

Difference between the daily maximum and minimum, on days with at least 18 hourly readings. Bizerte, which logs every two hours, has no such days and is left out.

```{r daily-range}
eda$temp_variability %>%
  transmute(Station = city, `Full days` = full_days,
            `Mean daily range (°C)` = avg_daily_range,
            `Largest daily range (°C)` = max_daily_range) %>%
  kable()
```

## 5. Daily cycle

```{r peak-hours}
eda$peak_hours %>%
  transmute(Station = city,
            `Warmest hour` = sprintf("%02d:00", warmest_hour),
            `Coldest hour` = sprintf("%02d:00", coldest_hour)) %>%
  kable()
```

![](output/figures/03_daily_cycle.png)

## 6. Correlations

Pearson correlation between hourly values, all available data per station.

```{r correlations}
eda$correlations %>%
  transmute(Station = city,
            `Temperature / humidity` = temp_humidity,
            `Temperature / solar` = temp_solar,
            `Temperature / wind` = temp_wind) %>%
  kable()
```

Humidity is strongly and negatively linked to temperature everywhere: relative humidity drops when the air warms up during the day. Temperature and wind are moderately positive, consistent with winds picking up during the warmer afternoon hours.

## 7. Extremes

```{r extremes}
eda$extreme_events %>%
  transmute(Station = city,
            `Hottest (°C)` = hottest_temp, When = format(hottest_time, "%d %b %H:%M"),
            `Coldest (°C)` = coldest_temp, `When ` = format(coldest_time, "%d %b %H:%M"),
            `Strongest wind (m/s)` = strongest_wind, `When  ` = format(strongest_wind_time, "%d %b %H:%M")) %>%
  kable()
```

All three stations recorded their coldest hour on the mornings of 10 and 11 December, which points to a regional cold spell rather than a local effect.
